plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the Microsoft Privacy dashboard, focusing on data visibility, control mechanisms (toggles/deletion), and feedback loops across desktop and mobile viewports.
plan.summary: The run will proceed from the main Privacy Dashboard to exercise the three available sub-pages: Browse History, Ad Settings, and Download Data. It will validate critical user flows including filtering activity logs, toggling privacy settings with visual feedback, and navigating the multi-step data download wizard. Special attention will be paid to modal confirmations for destructive actions and mobile tap-target accessibility given the prescan warnings.
assumptions: The 'Privacy Checkup' and other placeholder links (#) on the index page are non-functional or out of scope for this specific file set.
The 'Saving.../Saved' state changes on toggles are simulated via client-side JS as indicated in the site summary.
Destructive actions (Clear All) trigger modals that must be interacted with to complete the flow.
risk_hotspots: index.html: Global toggle list (verify 'Saving...' vs 'Saved' state feedback)
browse-history.html: 'Clear all' button (verify modal confirmation and cancellation path)
ad-settings.html: Master toggle dependency (verify if sub-toggles disable when master is off)
download-data.html: Multi-step form validation (ensure step progression logic works)

phases.title: Dashboard Overview & Global Controls
phases.objective: Validate the landing page structure, navigation integrity, and global privacy toggles.
key_checks: Verify top-level navigation links (Home, Devices, etc.) are clickable.
Interact with at least two global privacy setting toggles to observe 'Saving...' -> 'Saved' transition.
Check responsiveness of the activity data card grid.
exit_criteria: Global toggles show state change feedback.
No broken links in the primary header/nav.

phases.title: Activity Management (Browse History)
phases.objective: Test the detailed view for browsing activity, including filtering and deletion workflows.
key_checks: Navigate from Index 'Manage browse activity' link.
Use 'Time range' and 'Device' filters to verify table updates.
Click 'Clear all browse history' to trigger the confirmation modal.
Cancel the modal action to ensure data remains intact.
Attempt to delete a single row item.
exit_criteria: Filters apply correctly to the activity table.
Modal appears and blocks interaction until resolved.
Cancellation returns user to the list view safely.

phases.title: Ad Preferences & Dependencies
phases.objective: Explore the hierarchy of ad settings and test master/sub-toggle dependencies.
key_checks: Toggle the master 'See ads that interest you' switch.
Observe if sub-service toggles (Bing, LinkedIn, Xbox) become disabled or visually dimmed.
Re-enable master toggle and verify sub-toggles restore interactivity.
Check individual service toggles for independent state persistence.
exit_criteria: Master toggle clearly controls the enabled/disabled state of child inputs.
Visual hierarchy distinguishes between active and inactive settings.

phases.title: Data Export Wizard
phases.objective: Walk through the 'Download your data' multi-step process to check form continuity.
key_checks: Select specific data categories (e.g., only 'Browse activity').
Proceed through steps 1-4 (Include, Time range, Delivery, Confirm).
Verify breadcrumb or step indicator updates correctly.
Test 'Back' navigation between steps if available.
exit_criteria: User can progress through all 4 steps without error.
Selections made in Step 1 persist or are summarized in later steps.

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Repeat critical checks on mobile viewport to address prescan tap-target warnings.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport (e.g., iPhone SE/Pixel 5).
Verify hamburger menu or nav collapse behavior.
Attempt to tap 'Manage browse activity' and global toggles (check for overlap/mis-clicks).
Verify table readability in Browse History (horizontal scroll vs stacking).
exit_criteria: All primary controls are tappable without zooming.
Content reflows legibly without horizontal overflow issues.

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 4 HTML files provided in the site directory.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible toggles, filters, modals, and wizard steps.
coverage_targets.mobile: Perform full pass on Index and Browse History pages in mobile viewport.

notes: Prescan indicates small tap targets (<44px) in the global header; prioritize checking these in Phase 5.

The 'Search history', 'Location', and other cards on Index.html do not have dedicated HTML files in the prescan; treat their 'Manage' links as dead ends or placeholders unless they reveal hidden DOM content.
Focus heavily on the 'Saving...' state simulation in Phase 1 as it's a key UX feedback mechanism mentioned in the summary.
